Bluesheet for interim-2026-dkim-06
========================================================================

10 attendees.


Pete Resnick	
Murray Kucherawy	
Todd Herr	
Emanuel Schorsch	
Allen Robinson	
Trent Adams	
Wei Chuang	
Bron Gondwana	
Brian Godiksen	
Richard Clayton

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Good morning/afternoon/evening.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: This part made your chair (without his chair hat on) quite happy.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Claude is such a helpful chap.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: my code now treats non-VSDM as "leave the headers untampered, just forward on

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: "I haven't read the draft, but I have thoughts..." :rolling_on_the_floor_laughing::rolling_on_the_floor_laughing:

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: -- co-author

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: So provisional is cryptographically valid, and VSDM is properly chained?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Maybe such titles would be more clear.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Maybe I prefer "Validly Signed" and "Validly Chained". But that is strictly an editorial comment.

chat.author: Emanuel Schorsch
chat.text:
"If a message is not the initial form of a message (that is, it
   already contains DKIM2-Signature or Message-Instance header fields)
   then a Signer MUST NOT sign the message unless it is a Validly Signed
   DKIM2 Message (see Section 13), or there is an out-of-band
   arrangement covering the situation (see Section 12.3)." this is the part that I thought could be clearer that you shouldn't extend the chain

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: I think Emanuel just volunteered to write some suggested replacement text. :wink:

chat.author: Emanuel Schorsch
chat.text: Yes I'll send some suggested text out

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: What this discussion is also telling me is that we need to at least give enough time for  everyone to read -07 before we do a WGLC.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: My claude found this easy enough

chat.author: Brian Godiksen
chat.text:
Trying here - I noticed that based on spec07 - this would not be a relaxed domain match in DKIM2 signature. That surprised me. Is this expected?
header.From: noreply@example.com
mf= return@bounce.example.com
DKIM2 i=1 d=dkim.example.com

chat.author: Brian Godiksen
chat.text: Basically the From matches are "one way" down stream

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: It works fine, I also hate it -- it's almost an argument for not doing JSON since it's not 8-bit clean and just base64 encoding all header names and lines.  But I don't mind so much

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: I would not be surprised if someone yelps about it during Last Call, but if it works that's good enough for me.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Why retire the DKIM2 registries?

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: sorry, the DKIM registries?

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Time check: We're just past half done.

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: Punting this to "local policy" is an awful idea

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Punting what is the awful idea?

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: The decision on whether a change is ok enough to not require a From rewrite

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: I am not convinced that answering that question is specifiable.

chat.author: Emanuel Schorsch
chat.text: No body recipe is not the only reason for DMARC. Phishing is also just much easier if you don't modify your fromHeader and change the body to a phishing link.

chat.author: Emanuel Schorsch
chat.text: Reputation systems will generally be reactive. And reactive is not a good position to be in for phishing. It works for spam. Phishing less so.

chat.author: Allen Robinson
chat.text: The spec is going to either say local policy defines what changes are acceptable, or nothing is acceptable. DKIM1 enforces the latter. The future permitted changes header field could loosen that, but I don't think we should start all-open and use permitted changes to restrict.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Do remember that as a mailbox provider, you can always decide that you will undo the recipes and only show the user the original message.

chat.author: Emanuel Schorsch
chat.text: Yes, but it's a question of defaults. Right now the default is showing the current fromHeader and fromHeader rewriting. Should we overnight change those defaults to allow no fromHeader rewriting and wait for mailboxes to catch up and show the original message? Or should we leave the defaults and allow mailbox providers to restore the unmunged fromHeader pre-mailing list.

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: (one slide remaining)

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Time check: 30 minutes left.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: @Emanuel Schorsch I do think that is an operational question, not a spec question. If the big mailbox providers don't present original messages, they're going to reject them and mailing lists will continue munging From. If they stop rejecting them, mailing lists will start leaving From alone.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Re: the AND/OR discussion: I am remembering Peter Saint-Andre's comments about not leaving foot-guns laying around.

chat.author: Emanuel Schorsch
chat.text:
@Pete Agreed that ultimately that's how it will play out. But I   still don't think it's a good idea for the spec to default to an insecure posture. DMARC already has an operational carve out with local policy so that will continue to work. 
But a new mailbox implementing the spec should default to the safe posture.

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: @Emanuel Schorsch I suspect that the discussion is complicated enough to belong in the BCP, not the spec. But that's just me.

chat.author: Richard Clayton
chat.text:
to Brian's question, no you can't do that ... you need d=example.com
chatty bit from spec: "The aim is to allow a Signing Domain to be able to sign not only for itself but also for sub-domains."

chat.author: Brian Godiksen
chat.text: Wanted to make sure that outcome was intentional

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Is Content-Length actually appearing anywhere legitimate?

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: "A diff in your DOM" sounds uncomfortable.

chat.author: Brian Godiksen
chat.text: I have an implementation that should be launching in the next few days

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Time check: 5 minutes.

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: I'll do a review of my Authentication-Results draft to see what to change for -07

chat.author: Bron Gondwana
chat.text: Thanks all!
